correctness.rationale: From the exchange-block structure both squared main diagonals collect the same six squares, the three diagonal entries of X and of Y. Checked the six polynomial vectors against Choudhry §3.1 p. 7 and expanded independently in exact polynomial arithmetic, subtracting 2[(t^4+30t^2+9)(t^2+3)^2]^2. The coefficient list gives the frozen factorization, with defect -45339266 at t=2. The six ordinary entries sum identically to zero, so both ordinary diagonals equal the zero row sum. Monicity implies any rational Q-root is integral; exact reduction gives Q(t) mod 3 = t^14 and Q(3t) mod 3^8 = 2187, excluding all roots, including t=0. The other factor t^2+3 cannot vanish over Q. In both diagonal-minus-row square sums for aM+bJ (J all ones), the linear and constant contributions cancel, leaving a² times the original defect; a=0 is expressly excluded. Replay recipe: transcribe x11,x22,x33,y11,y22,y33 from Eq. (3.17)'s coefficient vectors, compute sum(entry^2) minus twice F² by polynomial expansion, divide by -2(t²+3), and reduce the quotient and its t→3t substitution in the indicated residue rings. Frozen VERIFICATION.md and verify.py were inspected, not executed. No exclusion over algebraic extensions or for other order-six families.

value.rationale: Whether the new explicit order-six pseudo-bimagic construction can be upgraded by specializing its parameter is an immediate and motivated question, particularly because general order-six parametrization remains open in the motivating paper. The exact invariant closes this route for all rational points, not just generic or small integers, and explains why affine normalization cannot help. This is a family-specific obstruction, not nonexistence of order-six bimagic squares.
